title: Library Bonds
text: Shall Bernalillo County, New Mexico, be authorized to issue its general obligation bonds, in one series or more, in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding $2,500,000 for the purpose of purchasing materials and resources for libraries within Bernalillo County, New Mexico, said bonds to be payable from general (ad valorem) taxes, and to be issued and sold at such time or times and upon such terms and conditions as the Board of County Commissioners may determine and as permitted by law?

title: Public Safety Gross Receipts Tax Dedication Update
text: Shall the City of Albuquerque amend the Public Safety Gross Receipts Tax to divide funds amongst updated city services? The money would be divided as follows: Police 35%; Fire 38%; Albuquerque Community Safety 8%; Health, Housing, and Homelessness 8%; Prisoner Transport 6%; and Code Enforcement 5%. This would not increase the tax rate.

title: City of Little Flock Special Election
text: An ordinance levying an additional one percent (1%) Sales and Compensating Use Tax within the City of Little Flock, Arkansas, to be used for general operational purposes; prescribing other matters relating to the levy; and for other purposes.

title: City of Siloam Springs Special Election: Bonds and Tax
text: Bonds of the City of Siloam Springs in the maximum aggregate principal amount of $55,000,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of extensions, betterments and improvements to the City's wastewater facilities, including particularly, without limitation, wastewater treatment plant and sewer collection infrastructure, and, in order to pay the bonds, the levy and pledge of a 0.625% local sales and use tax within the City. If the bonds are approved, there will be levied within the City a 0.625% local sales and use tax (the "Bond Tax"), the net collections of which remaining after deduction of the administrative charges of the State of Arkansas and required rebates will be used solely to retire or pay obligations with respect to the bonds in accordance with Amendment No. 62 to the Arkansas Constitution. The Bond Tax will expire after the bonds have been paid or provision is made therefor in accordance with Arkansas statutes. The Bond Tax will replace the City's existing 0.625% sales and use tax levied in 2018 for the purpose of retiring bonds to finance water improvements (the "2018 Tax"). The effective date of the Bond Tax will be the day following the date that the 2018 Tax expires. Proceeds of the bonds may fund a debt service reserve and pay expenses of issuing the bonds. The bonds may be issued at one time or in series from time to time.

title: County jails: transaction privilege tax of one-fifth of one cent (wording from the Board resolution, Section 3B; the printed ballot text may differ)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: COUNTY JAILS: TRANSACTION PRIVILEGE TAX OF ONE-FIFTH OF ONE CENT, the same rate as the existing jail facilities excise tax expiring in March 2027. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: Pursuant to authority granted by the State of Arizona, the County seeks voter approval of a transaction privilege tax set at the rate allowed under A.R.S. § 42-6109.02, section A, one-fifth of one cent to be used for county jail facilities and programs. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving a sales tax of one-fifth of one cent ($0.002) for county jail facilities and programs, the same rate as the current tax that is expiring. A “no” vote shall have the effect of rejecting a sales tax of one-fifth of one cent ($0.002) for jail facilities and programs.

title: Franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A MEASURE REFERRED TO THE PEOPLE BY THE CASA GRANDE CITY COUNCIL RELATING TO A FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR THE USE OF THE PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY IN THE CITY OF CASA GRANDE, ARIZONA FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ITS ELECTRIC UTILITY DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: SHALL A FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY BE APPROVED FOR A PERIOD OF 25 YEARS FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ITS ELECTRIC UTILITY WITHIN THE CITY RIGHTS-OF-WAY, IN THE FORM PROVIDED TO THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF CASA GRANDE. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to allow them to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within the City of Casa Grande. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not approving a franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company to allow them to use the City-owned public rights-of-way to construct, operate, and maintain its electric utility within the City of Casa Grande.

title: Eloy General Plan ratification
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: SHALL “ELOY GENERAL PLAN: PLANNING TODAY FOR A STRONGER TOMORROW”, AND ALL OF ITS ELEMENTS, BE RATIFIED AND APPROVED AS THE GENERAL PLAN FOR THE CITY OF ELOY? DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PROPOSAL TO THE VOTERS FOR RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF ELOY GENERAL PLAN: PLANNING TODAY FOR A STRONGER TOMORROW, AS ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL ON JUNE 2, 2026, RESOLUTION NO. 26-1660 THE GENERAL PLAN IS A STATEMENT OF LAND DEVELOPMENT POLICIES THAT SETS FORTH OBJECTIVES, PRINCIPLES AND STANDARDS FOR GROWTH AND REDEVELOPMENT. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of ratifying and approving the “Eloy General Plan – Planning Today for a Stronger Tomorrow”, and all of its elements as adopted by the City Council of the City of Eloy, Arizona, as the General Plan for the City of Eloy and shall become effective as provided by law. A “no” vote shall have the effect of keeping the current “City of Eloy General Plan Readoption, May 11, 2020”, in effect until a new General Plan is presented, ratified, and approved by the Eloy City Council and the voters of the City of Eloy, Arizona, as provided by law.

title: Extension of alternative expenditure limitation (sample shows official and descriptive titles only, with no question sentence)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A RESOLUTION PROPOSING AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF KEARNY. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PURSUANT TO THE ARIZONA STATE CONSTITUTION, THIS PROPOSAL ESTABLISHED AN EXTENSION OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF KEARNY FOR THE NEXT FOUR YEARS. ANNUALLY, THE TOWN COUNCIL WILL DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF THE ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE FISCAL YEAR AFTER AT LEAST ONE PUBLIC HEARING. THIS ALTERNATIVE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION REPLACES THE STATE-IMPOSED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION. A “yes” vote shall have the effect of extending the alternative expenditure limitation for the Town of Kearny. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not allowing the Town of Kearny to extend the alternative expenditure limitation and to require expenditures of the city to be limited by the state-imposed expenditure formula.

title: Permanent base expenditure limitation adjustment
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A RESOLUTION PROPOSING A PERMANENT BASE ADJUSTMENT TO THE 1979-80 STATE IMPOSED BASE LIMITATION FOR THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PURSUANT TO THE ARIZONA STATE CONSTITUTION, THIS PROPOSAL PERMANENTLY ADJUSTS THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY’S 1979-80 BASE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION BY $183,997,957 IN FISCAL YEAR 2028, INCREASING THE TOWN’S ESTIMATED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION TO $850,000,000. THIS PERMANENT BASE ADJUSTMENT MODIFIES THE STATE-IMPOSED EXPENDITURE LIMITATION AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE PROPERTY TAX OR SALES TAX. SHALL THE TOWN OF SAN TAN VALLEY, ARIZONA, PERMANENTLY ADJUST ITS 1979-80 BASE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION BY $183,997,957 BEGINNING IN FISCAL YEAR 2028? A “yes” vote shall have the effect of permanently adjusting the Town of San Tan Valley’s 1979-80 base expenditure limitation by $183,997,957, in fiscal year 2028, increasing the Town’s base expenditure limitation to $850,000,000, which will then continue to grow annually based on population and inflation. A “no” vote shall have the effect of not allowing the Town of San Tan Valley to adjust its base adjustment limit, and the Town continue to be subject to the existing state-imposed expenditure limitation and may be legally prohibited from spending the revenues it receives and appropriates through the annual budget process.

title: Franchise agreement with Arizona Public Service Company
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: A MEASURE SUBMITTED TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE TOWN OF FLORENCE BY THE FLORENCE TOWN COUNCIL RELATING TO THE PROPOSED GRANT OF A NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR THE USE OF PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY WITHIN THE TOWN OF FLORENCE, ARIZONA, FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONSTRUCTING, OPERATING, AND MAINTAINING ELECTRIC UTILITY FACILITIES. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: CONSIDERATION OF A PROPOSED NONEXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT WITH ARIZONA PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY FOR A TERM OF 25 YEARS ALLOWING USE OF PUBLIC RIGHTS-OF-WAY WITHIN THE TOWN OF FLORENCE TO CONSTRUCT, OPERATE, AND MAINTAIN ELECTRIC UTILITY FACILITIES. Shall a nonexclusive franchise be granted to Arizona Public Service Company, in the form of the proposed franchise agreement filed with the Town Clerk and published as required by law, for a term of 25 years, authorizing Arizona Public Service Company to use public rights-of-way within the Town of Florence to construct, operate, and maintain electric utility facilities? A “yes” vote shall have the effect of approving the grant of a nonexclusive franchise agreement to Arizona Public Service Company, in the form filed and published, authorizing Arizona Public Service Company to use public rights-of-way within the Town of Florence for a 25-year term to construct, operate, and maintain electric utility facilities. title: Maricopa General Plan ratification (“Advancing Maricopa”)
text: OFFICIAL TITLE: RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: PROPOSED RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN, PURSUANT TO A.R.S. § 9-461.06, AS SET FORTH IN RESOLUTION 26-10 ADOPTING “ADVANCING MARICOPA,” THE CITY OF MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN AND LAND USE MAP, APPROVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA ON JUNE 2, 2026. THE GENERAL PLAN PROVIDES DIRECTION FOR DEVELOPMENT, CONSERVATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE INVESTMENTS IN THE CITY. IT DOES NOT CHANGE ANY CURRENT ZONING OR RAISE ANY TAXES. SHALL “ADVANCING MARICOPA,” THE MARICOPA GENERAL PLAN AND LAND USE MAP, AS ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL ON THE 2ND DAY OF JUNE 2026, BE APPROVED BY THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE CITY OF MARICOPA. A yes vote shall have the effect of approving “Advancing Maricopa,” the Maricopa General Plan and Land Use Map as adopted by the City Council and it shall become effective as provided by law. A no vote shall have the effect of leaving the Maricopa 2016 General Plan in place until such time as Council shall adopt other provisions which may be ratified by the voters.

title: $39,000,000 general obligation bonds
text: SHALL COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 OF PINAL COUNTY, ARIZONA (THE “DISTRICT”), BE ALLOWED TO ISSUE AND SELL GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS IN THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF NOT TO EXCEED $39,000,000 TO PROVIDE MONEY FOR THE FOLLOWING PURPOSES: • CONSTRUCTING AND/OR PURCHASING SCHOOL BUILDINGS; • RENOVATING SCHOOL BUILDINGS; • PURCHASING PUPIL TRANSPORTATION VEHICLES; • ACQUIRING BY PURCHASE OR LEASE SCHOOL LOTS; • IMPROVING SCHOOL GROUNDS, INCLUDING ADJACENT WAYS THERETO; • SUPPLYING SCHOOL BUILDINGS WITH FURNITURE, EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY; • LIQUIDATING INDEBTEDNESS INCURRED FOR THE PURPOSES SET FORTH HEREIN; • PROVIDING ALL UTILITIES AND OTHER CAPITAL ITEMS NECESSARY FOR THE CONSTRUCTION AND RENOVATION OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS AND FOR IMPROVING SCHOOL GROUNDS; • PAYING ALL ARCHITECTURAL, DESIGN, ENGINEERING, PROJECT AND CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN CONNECTION WITH THE PURPOSES SET FORTH ABOVE; AND • PAYING ALL LEGAL, FINANCIAL AND OTHER COSTS IN CONNECTION WITH ISSUANCE OF THE BONDS? THE BONDS WILL BEAR INTEREST AT RATES NOT EXCEEDING 12% PER YEAR. INTEREST MAY BE EVIDENCED BY SEPARATE CERTIFICATES AND WILL BE PAID ON JANUARY 1 AND JULY 1 EACH YEAR UNTIL THE BONDS MATURE. THE BONDS, AND ANY BONDS ISSUED TO REFUND THE DISTRICT’S BONDS, MAY BE SOLD AT PRICES THAT INCLUDE PREMIUMS NOT GREATER THAN PERMITTED BY LAW. THE BONDS MAY BE REFUNDED BY THE ISSUANCE OF REFUNDING BONDS OF A WEIGHTED AVERAGE MATURITY OF LESS THAN 75% OF THE WEIGHTED AVERAGE MATURITY OF THE BONDS BEING REFUNDED. BONDS WILL BE IN THE DENOMINATIONS OF $5,000 EACH OR IN MULTIPLES OF $5,000 AND WILL MATURE ON THE FIRST DAY OF JANUARY AND/OR JULY IN YEARS DETERMINED BY THE DISTRICT’S GOVERNING BOARD. THE BONDS SHALL MATURE OVER A PERIOD OF NOT (I) LESS THAN ONE (1) YEAR (OR A PORTION THEREOF) OR (II) MORE THAN TWENTY (20) YEARS FROM THE DATE OF THEIR ISSUANCE. THE ISSUANCE OF THESE BONDS WILL RESULT IN A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE SUFFICIENT TO PAY THE ANNUAL DEBT SERVICE ON BONDS. THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS THAT ARE PROPOSED TO BE FUNDED THROUGH THIS BOND ISSUANCE ARE TO EXCEED THE STATE STANDARDS AND ARE IN ADDITION TO MONIES PROVIDED BY THE STATE. COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 IS PROPOSING TO ISSUE CLASS B GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS TOTALING $39,000,000 TO FUND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS OVER AND ABOVE THOSE FUNDED BY THE STATE. UNDER THE STUDENTS FIRST CAPITAL FUNDING SYSTEM, COOLIDGE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 21 IS ENTITLED TO STATE MONIES FOR NEW CONSTRUCTION AND RENOVATION OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN ACCORDANCE WITH STATE LAW. A “yes” vote shall authorize the Coolidge Unified School District No. 21 of Pinal County, Arizona governing body to issue and sell $39,000,000 of school improvement bonds of the district to be repaid with secondary property taxes. A “no” vote shall not authorize the Coolidge Unified School District No. 21 of Pinal County, Arizona governing body to issue and sell such bonds of the district.

title: Maintenance and operation budget override continuation
text: SHALL THE GOVERNING BOARD OF MARICOPA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 20 OF PINAL COUNTY, ARIZONA (THE “DISTRICT”), ADOPT A GENERAL MAINTENANCE AND OPERATION BUDGET THAT INCLUDES AN AMOUNT THAT EXCEEDS THE REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT SPECIFIED BY STATUTE BY 10% FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 AND FOR SIX (6) SUBSEQUENT YEARS AS DESCRIBED BELOW? THE FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 BUDGET OVERRIDE AUTHORITY REPRESENTS AN EXTENSION OF THE EXISTING BUDGET OVERRIDE AUTHORITY WHICH IS SCHEDULED TO PHASE DOWN BY ONE-THIRD FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028, BY ANOTHER ONE-THIRD FOR FISCAL YEAR 2028/2029, AND WILL TERMINATE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2029/2030 IF THE VOTERS DO NOT APPROVE THE OVERRIDE. THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED CONTINUATION OF THE BUDGET INCREASE OF THE PROPOSED BUDGET OVER THE ALTERNATE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027/2028 IS ESTIMATED TO BE $2,758,048. IN FISCAL YEARS 2027/2028 THROUGH 2031/2032 THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED INCREASE WILL BE 10% OF THE DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT IN EACH OF SUCH YEARS, AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 15-481(P) OF THE ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES. IN FISCAL YEARS 2032/2033 AND 2033/2034, THE AMOUNT OF THE PROPOSED INCREASE WILL BE 6.67% AND 3.33%, RESPECTIVELY, OF THE DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT IN EACH OF SUCH YEARS, AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 15-481(P) OF THE ARIZONA REVISED STATUTES. ANY BUDGET INCREASE CONTINUATION AUTHORIZED BY THIS ELECTION SHALL BE ENTIRELY FUNDED BY A LEVY OF TAXES ON THE TAXABLE PROPERTY IN THIS SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR THE YEAR FOR WHICH ADOPTED AND FOR SIX (6) SUBSEQUENT YEARS, SHALL NOT BE REALIZED FROM MONIES FURNISHED BY THE STATE AND SHALL NOT BE SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATION ON TAXES SPECIFIED IN ARTICLE IX, SECTION 18, CONSTITUTION OF ARIZONA. BASED ON THE CURRENT NET ASSESSED VALUATION USED FOR SECONDARY PROPERTY TAX PURPOSES, TO FUND THE PROPOSED CONTINUATION OF THE INCREASE IN THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S BUDGET WOULD REQUIRE AN ESTIMATED CONTINUATION OF A TAX RATE OF $1.39 PER ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS OF ASSESSED VALUATION USED FOR SECONDARY PROPERTY TAX PURPOSES AND IS IN ADDITION TO THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S TAX RATE THAT WILL BE LEVIED TO FUND THE SCHOOL DISTRICT’S REVENUE CONTROL LIMIT ALLOWED BY LAW. A “yes” vote shall authorize the Maricopa Unified School District No. 20 School District Governing Board to continue the existing maintenance and operation budget override authority and resulting tax, which includes an amount that exceeds the District’s revenue control limit. A “no” vote shall not authorize the Maricopa Unified School District No. 20 School District Governing Board to extend the existing maintenance and operation budget override authority and resulting tax.

title: Sales and Use Tax Referendum
text: I approve a special sales and use tax in the amount of one-half (1/2) of one percent to be imposed in Charleston County for not more than twenty-five (25) years, or until a total of $4,250,000,000 in resulting revenue has been collected, whichever occurs first. The sales tax proceeds will be used to fund the following projects: Project (1) $2,702,000,000 – For financing the costs of highways, roads, streets, bridges, and other transportation-related projects facilities, and drainage facilities related thereto, that include: Featured Projects: Rivers Avenue Railroad Overpass at Durant Avenue, Mall Drive (S-790) Improvements, Patriot Boulevard Widening, Better North Bridge Pedestrian and Bicycle Improvements, Battery Extension West / Calhoun Street - Medical District, Hagood Avenue Improvements, Maybank Highway Southern Pitchfork and Roundabouts, Glenn McConnell Parkway at Magwood Road, US 17 South Widening from Dobbin Road to SC-162, Johnnie Dodds Boulevard at Houston Northcutt Boulevard and Wingo Way Improvements, Long Point Road Resiliency and Safety Improvements. Intersection Projects: Stall Road at Midland Park Road and Ashley Phosphate Road, Ladson Road at Palmetto Commerce Parkway, Ashley Phosphate Road at Cross County Road and Brandywine Road, US 78 at Limehouse Lane, Savannah Highway at Ashley Town Center Drive, Maybank Highway at Riverland Drive, Main Road at Mary Ann Point Roundabout, SC-162 at Salters Hill Roundabout, SC-174 at SC-164 Roundabout, Steed Creek Road at US 17 North, SC-45 at US 17 North. Whipple Road at Mathis Ferry Road and Lucy Beckham High School. Pavement Management: Resurfacing paved roads throughout Charleston County based on condition, traffic volume, safety requirements, and age of infrastructure, Rural Road Safety Program, Roadway Elevation Resiliency Program including Seabrook Island Road Project. Bike / Pedestrian Improvements: Bike and Pedestrian infrastructure throughout Charleston County, including but not limited to, Countywide Bike Ped Plan, Rivers Avenue Lowcountry Rapid Transit Last Mile Connections, City of Charleston Safe Streets for All Plan, Rethink Folly Road Plan, Mount Pleasant Way Plan. Other Projects: 2016 Sales and Use Tax Carryover Projects (Dorchester Road Widening and Palmetto Commerce Parkway Phase 3), Traffic Signal Synchronization, Reynolds Avenue Improvements, Noise Wall at Palmetto Commerce Interchange Project, and other future needs for highways, roads, streets, bridges, and drainage facilities. All featured projects, intersection projects, pavement management projects, and all other projects shall consider the inclusion of bicycle, pedestrian, and public transit access in the design process, as contextually appropriate. If any project listed above cannot be accomplished, the amounts of Sales and Use Tax associated will be applied to any other project listed above Project (2) $858,000,000 – For financing the operation and expansion of public transit systems operated by Charleston Area Regional Transportation Authority (CARTA) or jointly operated by the County and other governmental entities and the implementation of the Downtown Route Study. Project (3) $690,000,000 – For financing the costs of greenbelts with a 50% urban and 50% rural allocation of the revenues, including but not limited to, purchasing land for conservation, conservation easements, passive greenspaces, public parks, access points to waterways; and protecting natural resources, agricultural landscapes, heritage landscapes, scenic corridors and water resources.

title: Council member monthly compensation
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to authorize monthly compensation for members of the City Council in the amount of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) per month for the Mayor and five hundred dollars ($500.00) per month for Council Members?

title: Surveillance technology and AI framework
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to add a new section requiring the City Council to adopt protections governing the collection, use, retention, and oversight of data, facial recognition, and surveillance technologies, to establish transparent approval processes for such technologies, and to require a responsible artificial intelligence framework?

title: Ordinance adoption procedures
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise the procedures for adopting ordinances, including eliminating the requirement that a proposed ordinance be read at two Council meetings and instead requiring an additional reading only when the City Council determines that an amendment substantively changes the ordinance, and revising related notice and public-availability procedures?

title: Petition signature threshold reduction
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to lower, from fifteen percent (15%) to ten percent (10%), the percentage of qualified voters required to sign a petition for an initiative, referendum, or nonbinding referendum?

title: Council meeting and agenda procedures
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise City Council meeting and agenda procedures, including requiring that an item submitted by a Council Member with the support of a second Council Member be placed on an agenda within sixty (60) days, requiring the Mayor to include such items on the agenda, and clarifying the Council's meetings requirements with City-created boards and commissions?

title: Supplementary petition deadline
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to provide that voter petition requirements be completed in compliance with state law and extending, from two (2) weeks to four (4) weeks, the deadline to file a supplementary petition after a petition is certified insufficient?

title: Annual budget requirements
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise the requirements governing the development and content of the City's annual budget, including requiring that the City Manager prepare and present the budget in accordance with Government Finance Officers Association budget-award guidelines, requiring comparative budget information and a five-year financial forecast, and to add a new charter section requiring a publicly accessible reporting system and final close-out reports for major capital projects?

title: Mayor excuses city manager
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to authorize the mayor alone to excuse the City Manager from attending a meeting?

title: Non-voting ETJ advisory members
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to allow City Council to appoint residents of the city's ETJ as non-voting advisory participants on city boards and commissions?

title: Strategic direction and policy framework
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to provide that the Mayor and City Council set the strategic direction and general policy framework of the City?

title: Public comment during removal proceedings
text: Shall the City Charter be amended to allow public comment during removal proceedings without requiring City Council approval?

title: Municipal judge residency requirement
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to remove the requirement that the Municipal Court Judge reside within the City?

title: Public participation in council meetings
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to add a new Section 11.05 specifying how the public may participate in City Council meetings, including the submission of written comments on agenda items and participation by remote communication to the extent permitted by state law?

title: Non-substantive technical corrections
text: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to make non-substantive technical and conforming corrections, including standardizing capitalization throughout the Charter; adopting language conforming with state law, and amending or deleting language that is unnecessary or duplicative of state law?

title: Delete redundant charter language
text: Shall Section 4.1 of the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended to delete language which is redundant of and inconsistent with other sections in the Charter?

title: Councilmember indebtedness requirement
text: Shall Section 4.2 of the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended to delete the requirement that a Councilmember shall not be indebted to the City for consistency with state and federal law?

title: Council vacancy filling
text: Shall Section 4.4 of the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended to provide that, if a vacancy on the City Council occurs with twelve (12) months or less remaining in the unexpired term, the City Council may, by majority vote of the remaining members, fill the vacancy at the next regularly scheduled election?

title: Term limits for mayor and council
text: Shall the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended by adding Section 4.6 to impose term limits on the offices of Mayor and City Councilmember providing that no person may serve more than four terms in any combination of the office of Mayor or City Councilmember and that a person who has served four terms be permanently and for life ineligible to seek election or appointment to either office?

title: Councilmember powers and agenda
text: Shall Section 7.1 of the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended to provide that every City Councilmember, including the Mayor, has the same power and authority as every other Councilmember except where the Mayor is given explicit duties elsewhere in the Charter; that every Councilmember has the right to place any item on the City Council agenda; that an agenda item requested by a Councilmember must be added to the agenda and may not be refused by the City Manager or the Mayor; and that the City Manager and the Mayor have the authority to order the items on the agenda?

title: Executive session project disclosure
text: Shall the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended by adding a new Article requiring that, before the City Council takes final binding action on a matter deliberated in executive session under a project designation, code name, or other non-identifying reference, that before taking action a posted agenda item must provide enough specific information for the public to be made aware of the project including the name of the company?

title: Charter review commission
text: Shall the Charter of the City of Taylor be amended by adding a section requiring the City Council to appoint a Charter Review Commission at least once every ten years and providing a process for appointment and review?

title: Ratification of the 2026 General Plan Update
text: PROPOSITION 419 PROPOSAL SUBMITTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BULLHEAD CITY OFFICIAL TITLE: PROPOSED RATIFICATION OF THE CITY OF BULLHEAD CITY 2026 GENERAL PLAN UPDATE. A "YES" vote shall have the effect of approving the "City of Bullhead City 2026 General Plan Update" as adopted by the Mayor and City Council of the City of Bullhead City, Arizona and shall become effective as provided by law. A "NO" vote shall have the effect of keeping the current 2016 General Plan in effect until a new General Plan is presented and approved by the Mayor and City Council and the voters of the City of Bullhead City, Arizona as provided by law.
